note: Stress and opportunity rules for waterbodies. 'applies_to' lists the waterbody types a rule is checked for; 'gate' is an extra condition (for example a known zone of influence). Triggers use signal grades (true when above 0). Intensity runs from 0 to 100 and is scaled by the roles named in 'roles' (the highest of them), so a problem counts more where the water matters more. Rules are checked only for waterbodies that hold water in 3 or more of the 8 years and are not new (ctx_regular), except where noted.

rules.label: Inflow shortfall
rules.intensity: 100 * s_poor_fill * (0.5 + 0.5 * max(role_irrigation, role_drought_protection, role_fishery, role_livestock, role_recharge_domestic))
rules.rationale: The waterbody fills to a small part of its extent even in years without drought. A large catchment for its size (ctx_large_catchment) points to blocked inlet channels or diverted runoff; a small catchment (ctx_small_catchment) points to a waterbody too large for its catchment, where inlet works will not help.
rules.public_note: This waterbody fills only partly in the monsoon, even in normal years (s_poor_fill). If its catchment is large for its size (ctx_large_catchment), inlet channels may be blocked or runoff diverted; if small (ctx_small_catchment), the catchment may not produce enough runoff. Ask whether the inlet channels need clearing.
interventions: Catchment treatment where runoff is diverted
questions: Are the inlet channels of this waterbody blocked or broken?
Has runoff that used to reach it been diverted (roads, fields, other structures)?

rules.label: Poor retention
rules.rationale: Most of the water is gone by rabi. (Drying by summer is common in small waterbodies and is checked only where livestock depend on it.) On alluvium (ctx_alluvium) seepage is a likely cause; on hard rock (ctx_hard_rock) heavy drawdown for irrigation or leakage through the bund or sluice is more likely. Matters most where the water is needed in rabi or summer.
rules.public_note: This waterbody loses most of its water by rabi (s_dries_by_rabi). On alluvial soils (ctx_alluvium) this may be seepage; on hard rock (ctx_hard_rock) it may be heavy drawing for irrigation, or leaks through the bund or a damaged sluice gate. Ask whether the sluice gate holds water.
interventions: Rules for sharing and timing water draws
questions: Is the sluice gate or outlet damaged, so that water leaks out?
Does the bund leak or has it breached?
How many months after the monsoon does it hold water?

rules.label: Shrinking or silting
rules.intensity: 100 * s_shrinking * (0.7 + 0.3 * ctx_eroding_catchment) * (0.5 + 0.5 * max(role_irrigation, role_drought_protection, role_fishery, role_livestock, role_recharge_domestic))
rules.rationale: Relative to the tehsil's other waterbodies in the same years, kharif fill has fallen steadily over 2017-24. Siltation is the commonest cause, more likely where the catchment is sloping, has high runoff or degrading land (ctx_eroding_catchment). Encroachment of the bed is another; the census fields and community questions can separate the two.
rules.public_note: The share of this waterbody that fills in the monsoon has been falling year after year (s_shrinking). Silt from the catchment is a common reason, more so where the catchment is sloping or eroding (ctx_eroding_catchment). Desilting may restore storage; ask how deep the silt is and whether the bed is being cultivated.
questions: How much silt has built up in the waterbody?
Is part of the bed being cultivated or built on?

rules.label: Stopped holding water
rules.intensity: 100 * s_sudden_loss * (0.5 + 0.5 * max(role_irrigation, role_drought_protection, role_fishery, role_livestock, role_recharge_domestic))
rules.rationale: The waterbody filled well in 2017-19 but hardly at all in the last two years. A breached bund, a blocked or diverted inlet, deliberate draining or encroachment are likely; this needs a field check rather than a remote diagnosis.
rules.public_note: This waterbody used to fill well but has held little or no water in the last two years (s_sudden_loss). The bund may have breached, the inlet may be blocked, or the bed may have been drained or taken over. Ask what changed.
questions: Has the bund breached or the waterbody been drained?
Has the inlet been blocked or the bed encroached in recent years?

rules.label: Fails in drought years
rules.rationale: Kharif fill falls to half or less in the home MWS's drought years, where rainfed farming depends on it for protective irrigation. Deepening, catchment improvements or linking to a larger source raise drought resilience.
rules.public_note: In drought years this waterbody fills to half or less of its usual level (s_drought_failure), just when rainfed crops nearby need protective irrigation. Ask how crops fared in recent drought years and whether the water was shared fairly.
interventions: Deepening and desilting for more carry-over storage
Water sharing rules for protective irrigation in dry spells
questions: In drought years, could farmers get water from this waterbody for a protective irrigation?
How was the water shared in the last dry year?

rules.label: Water not reaching fields
rules.rationale: Water lasts into rabi, but cropping intensity in the zone of influence is low or falling. Distribution channels, fair-sharing arrangements or the absence of a water user group may be limiting use; this is a management opportunity rather than a water shortage.
rules.public_note: This waterbody holds water into rabi (s_water_lasts), but fields around it grow little in the second season (s_zoi_low_ci) or less than before (s_zoi_ci_decline). Field channels, sharing rules or a water user group could help farmers use the water.
interventions: Form or revive a water user association with sharing rules
questions: Who uses water from this waterbody, and how is it shared?
Are the field channels from the waterbody working?

rules.label: No summer water for livestock
rules.rationale: In a pastoral setting, the waterbody holds no water in summer, when animals depend most on surface water.
rules.public_note: Livestock graze in this area, but this waterbody holds no water in summer (s_no_summer_water). Deepening part of it, or a separate cattle trough fed from it, could keep drinking water for animals.
interventions: Deepen a section for dry-season storage
questions: Where do animals drink in summer?
Does this waterbody dry up before the summer months?

rules.label: Fishery opportunity
rules.rationale: Villages around it practise fishery, and the waterbody holds water into rabi, long enough for a fish crop.
rules.public_note: Villages here fish in community ponds (role: fishery), and this waterbody holds water into rabi (s_water_lasts). It may support fish rearing by a group, under the panchayat's lease rules.
interventions: Fish seed stocking by a group or cooperative
questions: Is this waterbody used for fishing, and who holds the rights?

rules.label: Too short-lived for fishery
rules.rationale: Villages around it practise fishery, but the waterbody loses most of its water by rabi, too early for a fish crop.
rules.public_note: Villages here fish in community ponds, but this waterbody loses most of its water by rabi (s_dries_by_rabi), too early for a fish crop. Better retention would help.
interventions: Improve retention (sluice and bund repair, deepening)
questions: Is fishing in this waterbody limited because it dries early?

rules.label: Short of canal water
rules.rationale: A canal-fed waterbody that fills poorly or loses water by rabi may be at the tail end of the canal, or getting irregular releases.
rules.public_note: This waterbody is fed by a canal but fills poorly or dries by rabi (s_poor_fill, s_dries_by_rabi). It may be at the tail of the canal or receive irregular releases. Ask when canal water arrives here.
interventions: Rotation schedule agreed with the irrigation department
Water user association at the outlet
questions: When and how often does canal water reach this waterbody?

rules.label: River drying in summer
rules.intensity: 100 * max(s_dry_season_decline, min(s_no_summer_water, s_shrinking)) * (0.5 + 0.5 * max(role_irrigation, role_livestock, role_recharge_domestic))
rules.rationale: The river stretch holds less water in summer over the years. Upstream extraction or falling groundwater (ctx_gw_stressed) reducing baseflow are likely causes; sand mining is another, not visible in the data.
rules.public_note: This stretch of river holds less water in summer than it used to (s_dry_season_decline). Pumping upstream or falling groundwater may be reducing its flow. Ask whether sand is being mined here.
interventions: Regulate pumping from the river in summer
questions: Has the river here started drying earlier in summer?
Is sand being mined from this stretch?
